content.title: About
content.content: Romaine lettuce is a variety of leafy vegetable cultivated for its dense, crunchy leaves with a mild, slightly nutty flavor. It is commonly used in fresh salads, sandwiches, and as a garnish. Romaine is sold as whole heads or pre‑shredded.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Romaine gets its name from the city of Rome, where it was grown in ancient times.
Its leaves are more robust and crisp than those of butter lettuce, making it a favorite for Caesar salads.
Romaine is about 95% water, contributing to its refreshing texture.
It provides vitamin K, vitamin A (as beta‑carotene), and folate.
Archaeological evidence shows that lettuce was cultivated in ancient Egypt.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting and supports bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Romaine lettuce is low in calories yet supplies dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and especially vital during pregnancy.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw lettuce can be contaminated with Salmonella or E. coli; thorough washing before consumption is essential.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional farming may use chemical pesticides; choosing organic or washing well reduces exposure.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergy to leafy greens, resulting in itching or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Romaine lettuce is typically eaten raw in salads, as a component of sandwiches, wraps, or as a garnish. It can be sliced into strips, chopped, or used whole. Before serving, rinse the leaves thoroughly and pat them dry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store romaine lettuce in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel and placed in a sealed bag. When stored properly it stays fresh for 5–7 days. Remove any wilted leaves to extend shelf life.
